dedupe_keys.name: nasa airspace concepts evaluation system aces gate to gate agent based simulation of aircraft operations in the us national airspace system

description: ACES is NASA Ames Research Center's fast-time simulation of the US National Airspace System, listed in the NASA Software Catalog (case ARC-15068-1). Contents: a dynamic, event-based simulation of aircraft operations from gate departure to gate arrival, built on a software-agent infrastructure that lets users configure custom simulations and explicitly model the command and control entities operating within the airspace system; its catalogue description frames it as a tool to test operational paradigms against growing air travel demand, congestion and delays. Producer: NASA Ames, developed for NextGen concept evaluation; the catalogue lists builds 7 and 8 from February 2013. Coverage: the US National Airspace System. Format and access: software released under a NASA software usage agreement as a U.S. and Foreign Release, requested through the NASA Software Catalog; no public download. Licence: NASA software usage agreement. Caveats: the code has not been updated since 2013, needs scenario and airspace adaptation data that the catalogue does not describe, and gives no system requirements. Simulation uses: network-level capacity and delay studies of airports and sectors, agent-based evaluation of traffic management concepts, and disruption scenarios for air transport resilience. Related records: NASA TRAC (model-nasa-trac-trajectory-based-route-analysis-control) and SOSS (model-nasa-soss-surface-operations-simulator-scheduler) cover route design and airport surface operations.
